items.title: Trump threatens to bomb Iran power plants in expletive-laden post
items.description: Donald Trump has threatened to attack Iranian energy and infrastructure in an expletive-laden social post, as part of a renewed warning to Iran to open the Strait of Hormuz by Monday.

items.title: One ship paid US$2m to pass Iran. Now we're looking at a new era
items.description: If Iran's idea of charging ships to pass through maritime choke points catches on, we are entering a new era of much more expensive, more dangerous global shipping.

items.title: 'Told my wife and daughter I was going to die': Christian villager relives Israeli attack
items.description: Bashir was injured when Israel attacked his home in a Christian village in Lebanon's south, where many residents refuse to leave despite threats of destruction.

items.title: US intelligence says Chinese satellite imagery of bases is helping Iran
items.description: A Chinese company's publication of AI-enhanced satellite imagery of US bases in the Middle East is helping Iranian forces identify targets, US intelligence believes.

items.title: UFOs over the oval: The sighting school kids were told not to talk about
items.description: Flying saucers, balloons or mass hysteria? It's 60 years today since Australia's biggest UFO sighting took place at a Melbourne school. Witnesses are still demanding answers about what happened that day.

items.title: Price crunch has some servo owners asking: 'Is it really worth doing this?'
items.description: Workers are reporting an increase in abuse from customers as service station owners say they're not making money from fuel price rises.

items.title: Japan assures Australia will get 'normal supply' of fuel
items.description: Fuel will continue to flow from Japan into Australia under assurances given during recent talks between the two countries.

items.title: The cleanest air on Earth holds a powerful lesson about our climate
items.description: Perched on Tasmania's wild north-west coast, Cape Grim has been quietly tracking the world's cleanest air for 50 years. Its data tell an interesting story about how our world has changed over half a century, including rare success stories.

items.title: How close a tree is planted can affect property prices, new report shows
items.description: Tree canopy coverage is being boosted in every capital city, but one micro-level analysis has found a link between property prices and the proximity of trees to houses.

items.title: Fiji cruise ship runs aground after hitting reef near 'Cast Away island'
items.description: Thirty passengers have reportedly been rescued after a cruise ship ran aground on a reef near the island where the film Cast Away was shot.

items.title: Dirty rentals are a 'common' experience for new tenants, but legal rights exist
items.description: Having to clean a new rental property before settling in is a common experience for renters, but landlords have obligations when it comes to rental cleanliness upon moving in.

items.title: Bulldogs down plucky Bombers but lose two more players to injury
items.description: The Western Bulldogs hold off an Essendon fight back to triumph by 34 points, but will sweat on the fitness of Artie Jones and Tim English, who both limped off at Docklands.

items.title: Raiders' season lurches towards disaster as Knights run riot
items.description: The reigning minor premiers are in freefall after Canberra slumped to a fourth-straight loss at the hands of a resurgent Knights outfit.

items.title: Lomax's false start adds to anticipation ahead of pro rugby debut
items.description: Fans will have to wait for Zac Lomax's Western Force debut, providing further intrigue about how the ex-NRL star will cope when he takes his first steps in professional rugby.

items.title: A great gift or unexpected curse? Reflections on life as a new retiree
items.description: While time is retirement's great gift, it can become a curse for anyone who has devoted decades to a career and then suddenly wakes up with relevance deprivation syndrome and no firm plan on what comes next, writes Matt Eaton.

items.title: Quiz: How well do you know your history?
items.description: Where was the Venus de Milo found? And what common household item first went on sale in April 1827?

items.title: How an 'experiential' class is helping older women's brains and bodies
items.description: Judy Taylor discovered dance later in life, but it has now become a source of joy, energy, and purpose.

items.title: The Kremlin's internet purge is like 'the Soviet era on steroids'
items.description: The Kremlin is increasing its efforts to dictate the narrative in Russia by shutting off the internet, restricting foreign messenger apps and punishing citizens for speaking out.

items.title: 'Abandoned': Sisters of officer slain by Dezi Freeman to sue Victoria Police
items.description: Leading Senior Constable Neal Thompson's sisters plan to launch legal action against Victoria Police over his death. They also say they felt "abandoned" by police after their brother's death.

items.title: Police look for missing cocaine after ocean 'drop-off' during 'bizarre' journey
items.description: Setting off from Panama just before Christmas, police say the MV Raider started its journey towards Sydney with almost 6 tonnes of cocaine aboard worth nearly $2 billion.

items.title: As reputation frays, Australia's $54b university brand faces a reckoning
items.description: A generation ago studying in Australia opened doors. Today rising costs and falling satisfaction are making international students think twice, and locals feel sidelined.

items.title: Terminal diagnosis hasn't stopped Joan Humble's final exhibition
items.description: After a lifetime of capturing Tasmanian landscapes, Joan Humble is holding her final exhibition. The 88-year-old has a terminal cancer diagnosis, but she is determined to keep painting as long as she can hold a brush.

items.title: Tim Tszyu dominates Denis Nurja to claim title in Wollongong
items.description: Tim Tszyu has won the WBO international middleweight title with a lopsided unanimous points win over Albanian Denis Nurja in Wollongong.

items.title: Kings break NBL trophy after dramatic overtime win as 36ers blow late lead
items.description: After trailing by six points late in regulation time, a dominant overtime display has earned the Sydney Kings a 113-101 victory in the fifth and deciding match of the NBL Finals.

items.title: Magnitude-5.5 earthquake 'morning wake-up call' to remote community
items.description: A remote community in the Anangu Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara (APY) Lands have woken up to rattling shelves and swinging lights caused by a magnitude-5.5 earthquake, Geoscience Australia says.
